epoch_millis() {
  local timestamp seconds nanoseconds milliseconds extra
  timestamp="$(date '+%s %N')" || return 1
  read -r seconds nanoseconds extra <<<"$timestamp"
  [[ "$seconds" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && -z "${extra:-}" ]] || return 1
  if [[ "$nanoseconds" =~ ^[0-9]{3,9}$ ]]; then
    milliseconds="${nanoseconds:0:3}"
  else
    # BSD date prints a literal %N. Second precision is conservative and keeps
    # deadlines and freshness receipts in the documented millisecond unit.
    milliseconds=000
  fi
  printf '%s%s\n' "$seconds" "$milliseconds"
}
deadline_ms="$(( $(epoch_millis) + timeout_seconds * 1000 ))"

Response to the review feedback quoted above.

**"The PR is a script portability fix, not the target task" / "`Fixes #49` is false"**: agreed. The earlier description overstated what the PR does. This PR does not complete #49. The retitled PR now says so at the top, and the closing keyword is gone. The earlier body still contained the phrase "resolve #49", so GitHub kept the issue linked for closing. I reworded it, and `closingIssuesReferences` for this PR is now empty, so merging it will not close #49. The #49 work that remains (owner-authorized `gdc ops site` / `gdc ops edge`, public inference acceptance, the DevShard v5 rollout, and the Gonka v0.2.16 transition) needs the owner-held `$HOME/.gdc-data/.env` and live infrastructure. I did not attempt it, and nothing here is deployed.

**"`epoch_millis` is duplicated in two places"**: fixed in 633608e by removing the helper completely. Both copies of `epoch-millis.sh`, the helper's test, the `install-ops.sh` change and the Makefile change are gone. Each call site now uses the bash builtin inline: `$(( ${EPOCHREALTIME//[!0-9]/} / 1000 ))`. The scripts already need bash ≥ 4, and every supported Host OS ships bash ≥ 5.1, so no shared file has to be deployed. The diff against `main` went from 17 files (+165/−31) to 12 files (+66/−31), with no new files.

**Why the change is needed at all** (checked, not assumed): the live `https://gonka-dev.net/status/gateway-health` currently reports `latency_ms` values like `19651863` and `23603745`. `date +%s%3N` prints unpadded nanoseconds under uutils coreutils 0.7.0 and 0.8.0. I confirmed this with the upstream release binaries. 0.8.0 is the `date` in the stock `ubuntu:26.04` image, and GNU coreutils and uutils ≥ 0.9.0 print 13 digits. `scripts/test-gateway-health-probe.sh` now reproduces this with a uutils-like `date` shim. The test fails against the `main` probe, which published `latency_ms: -1611246130079893093`, and passes on this branch.

**"Public pricing estimate: $32.635322 — a hint or a requirement?"**: neither. It is only an estimate of what the AI work session would cost if the same model (GPT-5.6 Sol) were billed directly at public API prices. It sets no budget or target for the change and says nothing about the issue's scope, so reviewers can ignore it when judging the PR.

**Verification**: `make shellcheck` passes. `GONKA_UPSTREAM_WORKTREE=<gonka clone> make test` passes except `test-recovery-contract`, which I skipped. It fails the same four assertions on unmodified `main` in this environment, so the failure is not caused by this PR. The `Net deployment runbook` workflow run for 633608e (run 36041471897) is waiting for maintainer approval because this is a fork PR.
